name: usage-gauge
description: Two rows under the prompt: model and effort chips in the Anthropic brand blue and orange (a symbol for the level), each turning the theme's warning colour and reading "selected → sent" when a main request does not send the model or effort you selected in /model, /effort, env or settings (checked at session start and on each request; subagents are not compared; between requests a new pick shows within 15 seconds in the plain colours); a click on the model chip types /model into the prompt box and a click on the effort chip types /effort, for you to send (never while the box holds words of yours), one clock chip with the session time, how long the prompt cache stays warm and the share of the main chat's input the cache served over the session (⏱ 1h 12m ⏳ 52m 96%: a dash before the first response, the theme's warning and error as the cache runs low, cold once its lifetime has passed; subagents' requests are not in the rate), cost, output speed, and a git chip: the branch, then three slots (↓ to pull, ± to commit, ↑ to push; a dim ?n for files git does not track yet); the session's folder starts the git chip (vault:main): the root's name, then › and the folder it moved into in the theme's warning colour (vault›mods:main), or outside the root its own name in the theme's error colour, read before each main tool call and every 15 seconds, sharing the chip's room with the branch, and its own item where there is no git chip; context, 5-hour and weekly limits as 10-cell bars in Claude Code's own bar colour (its warning from 70%, its error from 90%) with reset times; the context bar fills toward the point where auto-compaction runs (the whole window when it is off) and also shows the tokens held. Without a plan (an API key, a cloud provider) the 5-hour and weekly bars go once the first turn has ended with no window reported. The git chip only reads: git status every 15 seconds and after each turn, and a fetch every 5 minutes so ↓ is current (it writes git's remote-tracking refs, never your files). The folder and the branch take the room the drawn row leaves, 2 cells to spare, and are cut with … to fit. Each item on row 1 can be turned off in /config. Reads usage figures only; adds no tokens.

showTime.title: Session time
showTime.description: Row 1: how long the session has run, in the clock chip.

showCost.title: Cost
showCost.description: Row 1: the session's cost so far, at API prices.

showSpeed.title: Output speed
showSpeed.description: Row 1: tokens per second of the latest reply. With the git chip on, a pane narrower than 85 columns drops it to make room.

showGit.title: Git slots
showGit.description: Row 1: the branch, then ↓ commits to pull, ± files to commit, ↑ commits to push. Reads the repository the session sits in; draws nothing outside one.

showCache.title: Cache timer and rate
showCache.description: Row 1: how long the prompt cache stays warm, then the share of the main chat's input the cache served, in the clock chip after the session time.

showFolder.title: Folder
showFolder.description: Row 1: the session's folder before the branch: the root's name, then › and the folder it moved into, in the warning colour. Without the git slots, or outside a repository, it is its own item.

fetchRemote.title: Fetch the remote
fetchRemote.description: Run git fetch every 5 minutes so ↓ shows what the remote has now. A fetch writes git's remote-tracking refs and nothing in your working tree. Off: ↓ is as of your last fetch. Needs the git slots on.
